scenario.name: Microsoft DPAPI, SpecterOps & Elastic DFIR — DPAPI MasterKey Backup RPC & Browser/Vault Credential Theft (EID 4692 / 4693)
scenario.overview: Picture a sunlit grand hotel lobby with a polished marble concierge desk, a golden wall of numbered room-key hooks, velvet luggage carts, and brass elevator doors. Stepping up to the grand hotel concierge desk, a guest writes a cleverly worded forwarding note inside the open leather guestbook ledger. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the hotel concierge's station, then quietly copies a trusted access pass from the hotel concierge's station. The hotel switchboard call log catches an unexpected outside phone call triggered directly from a routine guestbook check-in entry. In this scenario (T1555.004, Microsoft DPAPI, SpecterOps & Elastic DFIR, DPAPI MasterKey Backup RPC & Browser/Vault Credential Theft , EID 4692 / 4693), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dPAPI Blob, then domain Controller MS-BKRP BackupKey RPC, then offline Decryption of Windows Vault. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering DPAPI Blob, then Domain Controller MS-BKRP BackupKey RPC, then Offline Decryption of Windows Vault, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on Sysmon Event 4663 correlated across the documented kill chain.
